correctness.rationale: Incidence counting gives the nonconstant singular value s=q^((d-1)/2). On the zero-sum space, the half-constant contrast has eigenvalue gamma=(v-1)2^p-k-q^d3^p, and each paired nonconstant singular space gives -2^p ± s(3^p-1), with multiplicity v-1 each. The plus mode has exactly one crossing. Gamma decreases from -1 for q>=3 and for (q,d)=(2,2). For binary d=3,4 I independently bracketed the transverse root and obtained rational upper bounds -15906713/15625000 and -125361721/500000000 for gamma there. For d=5,6,7 the listed rational witnesses give gamma lower bounds 88976967/250000000, 7416389/250000000 and 11390161/125000000, with the transverse mode strictly negative. Replay: /tmp/opencode/pg-incidence-independent-certificate.py uses a 10^-9 grid, with (m/10^9)^b <= A^a for each bare power A^(a/b), and integer square roots for s. This also checked the needed quarter-power/log inequalities. For d>=8 the Taylor witness p=4/2^d gives gamma>1.12-8/2^d-1.022>0 and s(3^p-1)<1; for binary d>=5 the normalized derivative comparison is positive up to sigma<1/4. Strict lower negative type follows by applying the integral representation of x^r (0<r<1) to Gaussian kernels on the distinct Euclidean representatives, which also excludes larger exponents once a zero mode occurs. At p=0 the hollow unit off-diagonal matrix gives strict negative type. The centered Gram rank gives the two endpoint dimensions, and distinct representatives give strict positive definiteness at each bandwidth including the endpoint. At the binary contrast root gamma'(0)=2^d log(4/3)-2 log 2, and the witness gives p=O(2^-d); the quadratic remainder is O(2^d p^2), yielding the claimed error. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.
